First, we substitute $u={x}^{4}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4{x}^{3}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u={x}^{3}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{4}$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $-\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{x}^{3}}{1+9{x}^{8}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{\infty }^{0}\frac{1}{1+9{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{1+9{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{x}^{3}}{1+9{x}^{8}}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{1+9{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}\frac{1}{1+9{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{3}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(3u)]}_{0}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{1}{12}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3u)]_{0}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{1}{12}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3a)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(0)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{12}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3a)]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)]=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)]=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/94ad95c4f0477ae2dd29538e6cfcbbd52cbd7eda5b1c29246c1b4967566a7341.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{x}^{3}}{1+9{x}^{8}}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{1}{12}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3a)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{12}\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{24}.\end{aligned}
$$
